records.query: Need the patient's electrocardiogram, Holter monitoring, and echocardiography results, as these are core examinations for detecting arrhythmia or structural heart disease to confirm cardiac syncope.
records.text:
- Echocardiogram findings:  - Normal left ventricular ejection fraction (74%)  - Normal wall motion  - Left atrial enlargement (volume index, 34.89 mL/m2)  - Uncertain diastolic function  - No significant valvular abnormality  - Pulmonary hypertension (mean pulmonary arterial pressure 32 mm Hg)
- ECG findings:  Image Title: Initial ECG  Image Description: Shows sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block (PR interval 360 ms), right bundle-branch block (RBBB) and left anterior fascicular block (LAFB). Wide QRS complex (120 ms), rSR in lead V1, and RS in lead V6 (deep and wide S waves ≥40 ms). Left axis deviation and qR in leads I and aVL, and rS in leads II, III, and aVF.
- 24-hour ECG monitoring:  Image Title: Continuous ambulatory ECG monitoring  Image Description: Shows sinus rhythm (average 60 beats/min), PR prolongation (360 ms) and third-degree AV block with minimum heart rate of 36 beats/min. Mobitz type I second-degree AV block with pause and junctional escape beat observed. No atrial/ventricular arrhythmia found.

bindings.label: Patient presented with dyspnea and syncope during exercise
Patient is in their 80s; medical history includes essential hypertension and Parkinson disease
For the past year, patient reported dyspnea on exertion and exercise intolerance, with difficulty walking more than 100m
Patient experienced syncope during a bicycle ride, with loss of consciousness for a few minutes followed by complete recovery
Physical examination: blood pressure 150/78 mm Hg; chest auscultation revealed normal breath and heart sounds without murmurs
ECG/Holter shows first-degree AV block with bifascicular block and intermittent third-degree AV block (minimum HR 36 bpm)
Echocardiography shows normal EF and wall motion, left atrial enlargement, and mild pulmonary hypertension
High-grade atrioventricular block (bradyarrhythmia) is the underlying cause of cardiac syncope
